newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali town tense after poll clashes.
newsitem.headline: Nepali town tense after poll clashes.

text.p: Nepali soldiers and police patrolled the western town of Nepalgunj on Sunday following clashes between rival political groups, local residents said.
A curfew has been reimposed in some areas of Nepalgunj, 500 km (312 miles) west of Kathmandu, from 2 p.m. on Sunday to 5 a.m. on Monday, officials said.
"Curfew has been reimposed in some areas of Nepalgunj...to keep the situation under control," a Home Ministry spokesman told Reuters.
On Saturday, 19 people were injured when workers of the ruling and opposition parties clashed during the first phase of local elections in the Himalayan kingdom.
Authorities imposed a night curfew, relaxed it for a few hours on Sunday morning and then clamped down again.
Nepal is holding elections for 4,000 village committees that will form local governments. The second phase of elections will be held on May 26.
The body of a Moslem was found in a market place in Nepalgunj on Saturday but officials could not confirm whether he was the victim of poll violence.
Nepalgunj, in the west of the world's only Hindu kingdom near the border with India's Uttar Pradesh state, has a relatively large Moslem population.
Hindus constitute 90 percent of Nepal's population and Buddhists form another seven percent while Moslems, Christians and other religious communities account for the rest.
A multi-party system was established in Nepal in 1990 after pro-democracy movements whittled down the king's absolute powers.
